picks.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
picks.rationale: He's Detroit's clear #1 target and Washington has been soft on receivers underneath all year, so 40+ yards is close to a floor for him. Both our simulation and his own track record agree here, which is the kind of clean signal we like on a top pick.

picks.name: Jonathan Taylor
picks.rationale: Taylor is the whole Colts backfield right now and Atlanta's run defense hasn't been able to slow anyone down. This is about as safe a floor bet as this slate offers — he clears 40 rushing yards almost every week regardless of game script.

picks.name: Drake Maye
picks.rationale: Maye's been slinging it all season and Tampa Bay's pass defense is beatable, so the number still likes him. We're a notch more cautious than the raw probability suggests, though — New England's line has been banged up (our OL-health flag caught it), so there's more sack/scramble risk than usual eating into his yardage.

passes.name: Quinshon Judkins
passes.reason: Our simulation loves him for 40+ rushing yards (91%), but the historical baseline model is a lot more skeptical (61%) — that's a big enough gap between the two models that we don't fully trust either one yet. Cleveland's backfield split with the other RBs still isn't settled, so we're staying away until usage is clearer.
